title: Dinteville (Langres) to the Duke of Nevers, 4 July 1592, BnF Français 3621 no. 116 f. 130 (DECODE R9451)

steps.what: DECODE R9451 image fetched with cookie; fr. 3621 found on Gallica (btv1b52524472n), ff. 127-131 viewed.
Checked f. 130 for the contemporary decipherment DECODE mentions: none; the postscript is clear French.
Found f. 128, a sibling Dinteville letter in the same signs with interlinear decipherment.
Transcribed 50 signs of the f. 128 second cipher line by eye.
One-sign-one-letter homophonic mapping with up to three null types, aligned to the interlinear (align.py).
NoAutopilot (cipher-lab) rebuilt a partial key from the f. 128 gloss aligned to the 1882 print and published word fragments of f. 130; rows h, delta, stemmed zero left open.
Alex Zarco (PR #24): diacritic-aware sign transcription of f. 128 (180 signs) and f. 130 (522 cipher tokens), keeping crosses and strokes as parts of signs.
PR #24: gloss re-read as 'dessendre a Gennes' (not 'dascendre a Geneve'); align.py test then gives exactly one key, only the leading double bar null.
PR #24: key extended to f. 130 by context; 514 of 522 tokens read, 0 emended, 8 open; every cipher run joins the clear text grammatically.
PR #24: blind transcription by a separate agent from crops and a shape legend, 95.6% token agreement, decodes to 97.3% of the reading.
Re-ran PR scripts here: measure 514/522; lexicon score -2.00/letter real key, -2.19 f. 128-only key, best of 200 shuffled keys -4.29 (median -5.37).
Gallica IIIF crops: f. 128 gloss 'a gennes' and the cipher under it; f. 130 L05, L06 opening and L14 opening agree with the transcription sign for sign.

Revue de Champagne XII p. 340 (archive.org revuedechampagne12pariuoft): f. 128 plaintext agrees with the decode (Gene, doivent partir, d'escorte); f. 130 only summarised from its clear text, dated 4 July.

Found f128_signs.txt used plain D for the tailed delta (a) in four places, so f. 128 decoded f for a with the final key; corrected D -> D+ in f128_signs.txt and key_f128.tsv after checking the image. f. 128-only key on f. 130 now -2.11/letter, 71% in words.

outcome.method: key recovered based on adjacent plaintext
outcome.method_basis: Key rebuilt from the contemporary interlinear decipherment of the sibling letter f. 128 by outside contributor Alex Zarco (PR #24), completing NoAutopilot's published partial key; verified here (re-run controls, image spot-checks, 1882 print of f. 128).
outcome.fraction_read_source: reading_f130.tsv against key.tsv via scripts/measure.py: 522 cipher tokens, '?' counted unread

gaps.detail: first sign unclear; decode ? i u s

outcome.notes: Cryptanalysis by Alex Zarco (PR #24) building on NoAutopilot's partial key; this project found the crib (21 Sept) and verified. Date corrected 3 -> 4 July 1592. Contribution here is verification, the date and the DECODE correction.

prior.where: NoAutopilot, github.com/noautopilot/cipher-lab ciphers/fr3621-dinteville-1592 (partial key and word fragments of f. 130, from late Sept 2026); f. 128 plaintext in Revue de Champagne XII (1882) p. 340

human: Outside contributor Alex Zarco (alejandrozarco) did the transcription, key rebuild and reading with an LLM and sent PR #24; the owner asked the model here to verify and write it up. Bourdeau found the f. 128 crib on 21 Sept.
